plan.summary: This work upgrades the existing cf-coach dashboard front end without touching backend APIs, data contracts, or adding dependencies. The implementation should focus on reducing wasted vertical space, making dense panels progressively disclosed, improving readability through typography and spacing, and polishing chart/hover interactions while keeping the current dark theme and existing API-oriented tests stable.

phases.name: UI foundation and safe refactor hooks
phases.description: Prepare `src/dashboard/dashboard.js` and `src/dashboard/dashboard.css` for interactive polish by introducing front-end-only state hooks and stable DOM markers needed for collapsible sections, sticky profile behavior, and custom tooltips, while preserving all existing API fetch flows and payload expectations.
acceptance: Dashboard still renders all current panels from the existing API endpoints with no backend or payload changes
No new npm dependency is added and only `src/dashboard/dashboard.js` plus `src/dashboard/dashboard.css` are modified
Render output keeps panel-level identifiers needed by current smoke tests such as profile, rating-trend, roadmap, tag-ability, rating-buckets, weak-analysis, next-problem, and submission-timeline
A front-end mechanism exists to support local UI state for expand/collapse and tooltip visibility without requiring page reloads
tests: Keep existing dashboard smoke test passing to verify all core panels still render from fixture-backed APIs
Add or update frontend unit tests to assert new DOM hooks or data attributes for interactive panels are present without changing API contracts
Run existing API/data tests to confirm no server-side behavior regresses

phases.name: Masonry layout and readability refresh
phases.description: Replace the rigid equal-height dashboard grid behavior with a masonry-style or independent-height layout so panels flow naturally and large left-side content no longer creates empty space on the right. In the same phase, increase base typography, enlarge section labels and chart labels, widen inter-panel gaps and panel padding, refine shadow/radius, add sticky profile bar behavior, and smooth hover transitions for panels and problem cards.
acceptance: On desktop widths at and above 1024px, panels no longer force equal row heights that create large blank areas beside taller panels
Body-level typography is visibly larger than before, with panel titles at least 20px and kicker or section labels at least 13px
Chart axis labels render at 13px or larger
Panel gap is increased into the 28px to 32px range and panel inner padding is increased into the 24px to 28px range
Profile bar remains visible with sticky behavior while scrolling through the page
Panel hover and problem card hover transitions are present and visually smoother than the current abrupt state changes
tests: Update frontend rendering tests to assert new layout or sticky-related class names and larger typography hooks where practical
Add browser or smoke assertions that the profile panel still renders correctly after layout refactor
Keep dashboard browser smoke test passing to ensure layout changes do not break full-page rendering

phases.name: Tag Ability progressive disclosure
phases.description: Change the Tag Ability panel so it shows only the top 10 tags by default and adds a dark-theme-consistent toggle control to reveal the full list and collapse it again. The feature should reduce dashboard height while preserving the same tag data source and ordering logic.
acceptance: Tag Ability shows only 10 items on first render when more than 10 tags exist
A visible toggle control allows switching between collapsed and expanded states
Expanded state shows the full sorted tag list and collapsed state restores the default top-10 view
If there are 10 or fewer tags, the panel remains fully visible without a broken or misleading toggle
The toggle styling matches the existing dark theme
tests: Add frontend unit tests verifying default render includes only 10 tag rows when more data exists
Add frontend unit tests verifying expanded render includes all tag rows and collapse restores 10
Retain existing tag sorting tests to confirm the progressive disclosure feature does not change ordering semantics

phases.name: Roadmap focused-stage disclosure
phases.description: Refine the Roadmap panel so it shows a focused window around the current stage by default: current stage plus the previous two and next two stages, with a control to reveal all stages and collapse back. The current stage must always remain visible and state styling for completed, current, and not-started stages must remain intact.
acceptance: When sufficient stages exist, default roadmap view shows exactly five stages centered on the current stage where possible
The current stage is always visible in the default collapsed state, including edge cases near the first or last stages
A toggle control switches between focused five-stage view and full roadmap view
Completed, current, and not-started visual states are preserved in both collapsed and expanded views
Full roadmap view still supports the complete 20-stage dataset without API changes
tests: Add frontend unit tests verifying default roadmap render shows a five-stage window around the current stage
Add edge-case tests for current stage near the beginning or end of the roadmap
Update existing roadmap render tests to confirm current, complete, and not-started classes still apply after introducing collapsed and expanded states

phases.name: Chart interaction and tooltip polish
phases.description: Upgrade the charts by adding a gradient fill beneath the Rating Trend line, increasing Submission Timeline point radius and hover growth, and replacing SVG `<title>` tooltips with a custom styled div tooltip system that matches the dashboard theme. This phase should keep all chart data geometry driven by the current API payloads and existing render pipeline.
acceptance: Rating Trend renders a visible semi-transparent gradient area beneath the line
Submission Timeline points render larger than before and enlarge further on hover
Chart hover information is shown through a custom styled div tooltip rather than browser-native SVG title tooltips
Tooltip content includes the same essential information currently exposed for rating points and submission points
Charts remain readable and interactive in desktop layouts down to 1024px width
tests: Update rating trend render tests to assert gradient markup is present and native SVG title tooltip usage is removed
Update submission timeline tests to assert larger point radius and hover-target metadata needed by custom tooltips
Add frontend tests for custom tooltip rendering logic and content formatting for rating and submission entries
Run dashboard browser smoke test to confirm the page still loads and renders charts end to end
